Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

myself pronoun

also by myself, to myself, I myself

classical

Cic. Att. 8.14.2: ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor

mē, mihi (reflexive)

pronoun: the ordinary forms of ego, used reflexively

myself (as object)

Latin has no separate reflexive for the first person: “I wash myself” is mē lavō, “with myself” mēcum. Many English reflexives are a plain verb in Latin: “I enjoy myself”, mē oblectō or simply gaudeō.

Other words

  • ipse, ipsa, ipsum — myself (for emphasis: I myself, in person)

    pronoun, intensive: genitive ipsīus, dative ipsī · classical · Plin. NH 8.6: ipse ego haec scrīpsī; Cic. Amic. 10: mē ipse cōnsōlor (Lewis & Short, s.v. ipse, Lael. 3.10)

    The “myself” of “I did it myself”: it agrees with ego, said or understood (ipse for a man, ipsa for a woman). With a reflexive, ipse in the nominative stresses the doer: mē ipse cōnsōlor, I console myself (no one else does).

  • per mē — by myself, unaided

    phrase: per with the accusative · also used · classical · Mart. 14.73.2: hoc didicī per mē dīcere; Traupman 285

Examples

  • ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor

    I talk to you as if I were talking to myself.Cic. Att. 8.14.2

  • sed nōn egeō medicīnā: mē ipse cōnsōlor

    But I need no medicine: I console myself.Cic. Amic. 10 (Lewis & Short)

  • vix mī ipse crēdēns Thȳniam atque Bīthȳnōs līquisse campōs et vidēre tē in tūtō

    hardly believing myself that I have left Thynia and the plains of Bithynia, and that I see you in safetyCatull. 31.5–6

  • ego ipsa sum, inquit, hīc hospita

    “I’m only a guest here myself,” she said.Cic. Att. 5.1.3

  • nōn enim concēdō tibi plūs ut illum amēs quam ipse amō

    For I won’t grant that you love him more than I do myself.Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.7

  • ipse ego haec scrīpsī et spolia Celtica dicāvī

    I wrote this myself and dedicated the Celtic spoils.Plin. NH 8.6

  • psittacus ā vōbīs aliōrum nōmina discam: hoc didicī per mē dīcere "Caesar, havē"

    The parrot: I shall learn other names from you; this I learned to say by myself: “Hail, Caesar!”Mart. 14.73.1–2

See also I, yourself, himself, oneself.
